readinessHtml:
INPATIENT ROTATION READINESS

For all inpatient rotations, it is highly recommended that you spend ½ day shadowing your predecessor before starting, as you are generally expected to hit the ground running on day one.

Shadowing is not an excused absence from your current rotation. Coordinate with your predecessor to shadow after hours or on a weekend to gain exposure to the service without interfering with your current rotation responsibilities.

Complete all required credentialing, EMR access, and facility access in advance of your start date.

Although PC/Chiefs are here to help and navigate, it is the incoming resident’s responsibility to ensure they are ready to begin the service. Confirm your readiness and any outstanding requirements with the program coordinator, chief residents, and service attending before the rotation begins, if needed.

Overview

Larkin South and Waterford are your primary PGY-2 inpatient consult rotations. They are merged — 2 PGY-2 residents cover both services together. Expect a high census, diverse patient mix (stroke, TBI, SCI, orthopedic, amputation), and a strong emphasis on daily rounding and team-based care.

Before rotating: contact current residents to schedule a ½-day observation and resident-to-resident patient sign-out.

📍 Site Details

  • EMR: Meditech (HMS Medhost) + WRS
  • Remote Medhost access: https://secure.larkinhospital.com/home/medhost
  • Remote clinical access: https://clinical.larkinhospital.com/ (requires VPN)

🔄 Coverage Rules

Both residents work together and cover BOTH services. No overlapping PTO — max 1 resident on PTO at a time. No PTO approved without a completed coverage form.

  • If 1 resident is on PTO, the other covers all patients at both Larkin South AND Waterford
  • Under extenuating circumstances, an EMG/ISS resident may be asked to cover
  • Lighter rotation demands mean you may be asked to cross-cover WPB VA or ISS at year-end

📝 Larkin South — Daily Workflow

1 Week Before Starting:

  • Get Medhost/computer access — email carlosp@larkinhospital.com or call (305) 284-7711
  • Download VPN Connect for remote access (ask IT)
  • Get parking pass from HR during Orientation (free Resident Lot next to Miami Neuroscience Center)

Daily Steps:

  1. Go to Larkin, 2nd floor
  2. Take the facesheet → scan with Notes app → send to all 3 ISS emails below
  3. Log into Medhost → "My Group List" → select patient
  4. Write vitals on facesheet → click Notes → H&P → write PMH
  5. Click "Ancillary Notes" → find PT notes (usually by Nelson) → write PLOF and CLOF
  6. Check case manager notes for discharge planning
  7. See patients, perform physical exams
  8. Write notes (Medhost + WRS)
  9. Text Dr. Diaz — he calls around 4 PM to discuss cases

Daily Patient List Email — send to ALL THREE:

  • medassistant@integrativespineandsportsfl.com
  • frontdesk@integrativespineandsportsfl.com
  • officemanager@integrativespineandsportsfl.com

Send from the Larkin PM&R Gmail account — not your personal email. If patient names are similar, add NAME ALERT in the email.

📝 Note Writing — LCH South

  • Write notes in HMS Medhost → copy entire note into WRS (paste into HPI section)
  • In WRS: add name under disposition, add diagnoses, add billing codes
  • Billing codes: New consults: Hospital 99222 | Follow-ups: Hospital 99232
  • Ask senior resident for current WRS password
  • HMS Medhost note tutorial
  • WRS tutorial

Finding therapy notes in HMS Medhost:

  • Follow-up therapy notes: Documents → Nursing → dropdown: PTA, OT, ST, CM (check both PTA and PT)
  • Initial eval + MBS: Documents → Sum/Assessments

📝 Waterford — Workflow

Before Starting:

  1. Contact Pedro Toro (don@waterford.care) in person at Waterford for PointClickCare EMR access
  2. Email Dunia Castillo (bom@waterford.care) to be added to daily census email list
  3. Dunia sends daily census emails at 9–11 AM (weekends: sent Monday morning)
  4. You are responsible for HMO insurance patients only

Daily:

  • Write all notes in Word → email to Dr. Stein (pjstein14@gmail.com) → call/text (516) 578-7814 to discuss
  • PT/OT notes: must be printed by therapist — PointClickCare has limited access
  • Someone must physically be at Waterford M–F

Waterford Building:

Floor Contents
Ground/1st Subacute patients (your patients), Admissions office (red book = HMO patient functional status)
2nd Long-term care
3rd Physical Therapy Main Gym, Team conference
4th Medical Records
- Parking: Any unassigned spot; park away from entrance, leave closer spots for visitors

This is a subacute (not acute) rehab facility. You are a consultant here — not the primary managing physician. Keep recommendations focused. Patients cannot tolerate 3 hours/day of therapy.

✅ Rotation Expectations

  • H&P within 24h of admission
  • Daily progress notes for all patients
  • Send patient list + facesheets to ISS emails daily (Larkin South)
  • Attend all required didactics
  • Complete FIM assessments
  • Participate in family conferences
  • Present at least one case conference

📚 Learning Objectives

  • PM&R consult documentation in inpatient and subacute settings
  • FIM scoring and functional outcomes measurement
  • IRF vs SNF vs home discharge criteria
  • Interdisciplinary team communication
  • Billing and coding basics for PM&R consults

⚠️ Tips & Pitfalls

  • Larkin South: check therapy notes before rounds — therapists drive the functional picture
  • Waterford: don't overstep — you're a consultant, not the primary managing physician
  • Coordinate PTO with your co-resident early; overlapping PTO is not allowed
  • Flag similar patient names prominently in all email communications
  • TKA/THA cases are most common on Mondays and Wednesdays

  • Ask yourself daily: "Why is this patient here? When are they ready to leave? Where are they going?"
  • Dress professionally — you are a guest; treat all staff with respect

Highly recommended before you start: Read the St. Anthony’s PGY-3/4 Rotation Guide for day-to-day workflow, documentation, and rotation tips.

Overview

St. Anthony's is a PGY-3/4 acute IRF rotation under Catholic Health Services in Lauderdale Lakes. You work with greater autonomy here — managing complex neurologic and orthopedic cases, leading IDT rounds, and supervising junior residents. St. Anthony's uses the same CHS system as St. Catherine's West.

Before rotating: Contact Ana Martinez at least 2 weeks in advance for credentialing paperwork. Your account from St. Catherine's West (same CHS system) will carry over but still needs activation at this site.

📍 Logistics

  • Address: 3487 NW 30th St, Lauderdale Lakes, FL 33311
  • Service: Acute Inpatient Rehabilitation
  • EMR: Wellsky (notes) + ECS (labs/orders)
  • Residents: PGY-3 and/or PGY-4
  • Schedule: M–F + 2 alternating weekends per month.
  • Dress: Professional attire or scrubs with name badge.
  • Census: Approximately 10–15 patients.
  • Parking: Free; show your ID to the guard at the gate - speak to the front desk security at SA, they can help register your car with security and then you can also park in the “Physician Reserved” spots on the left of the gate (there are usually cones). This parking is further away from St. Anthony’s entrance though.

👥 Key Contacts

Role Name Contact
Attending Thiago Queiroz, DO (205) 835-4655
Rotation Coordinator Ana Martinez amartinez@chsfla.com; (305) 439-7491

📅 Daily Schedule

  • Pre-round independently before attending arrives
  • Lead IDT team rounds
  • Supervise and teach junior residents on admissions
  • Team conference: Tuesday at 10 AM for all patients; Thursday at 10 AM for patients admitted since Tuesday. Overnight Thursday admissions may wait until the following Tuesday. Occasionally starts at 9 AM by Dr. Queiroz’s instruction. Confirm conference times with Dr. Queiroz.
  • Complete documentation daily before leaving

Weekend Schedule:

Day Responsibilities
Saturday Full patient list + all progress notes + new admissions
Sunday New admissions only — write H&P

🏢 Building Layout

  • 1st floor: Therapy gym, rehab support services
  • 2nd floor: Acute patient rooms (your patients)
  • 3rd/4th floors: St. Joseph’s Assisted Living Facility.
  • North building: St. John’s SNF; residents cover St. Anthony’s acute patients in the south building, not these other facilities.

📝 Practical Workflow

  • Arrange 1–2 hours with the outgoing resident for sign-out and workflow orientation. Keep updated PPD, influenza vaccination, and ACLS/BLS records available for onboarding.
  • Generally arrive around 8 AM; Dr. Queiroz’s rounding time varies. Coordinate with the outgoing resident and Dr. Queiroz/APRN. Both residents generally attend rounds and split the census.
  • Review the morning vital-sign log and establish patient stability, then prioritize new admissions before follow-ups.
  • Complete admission notes within 24 hours and progress notes the day the patient is seen.
  • Notes are in WellSky; orders and Tuesday labs are in ECS.
  • Work toward leading team conference independently by the end of the first month.
  • Verbally inform nursing/secretarial staff about STAT orders, labs, consults, and discharge medication reconciliation printouts. Provide discharge med-rec printouts for all patients except those going to SNFs.
  • Additional recommended reading: Cuccurullo, alongside Braddom.

✅ Rotation Expectations

  • Credential with Ana Martinez 2 weeks in advance
  • Lead IDT rounds daily
  • Supervise PGY-2 residents on admissions and note-writing
  • Manage complex neurorehab and orthopedic patients with increasing autonomy
  • Present at case conference
  • Complete midpoint and end-of-rotation evaluations in New Innovations

📚 Learning Objectives

  • Advanced spasticity management (oral agents, botulinum toxin)
  • Complex SCI and TBI rehab at the sub-acute/acute interface
  • Teaching and supervision of junior residents
  • Leadership in interdisciplinary teams
  • Managing medically complex rehab patients independently

⚠️ Tips & Pitfalls

  • You're expected to function more independently here — ask attendings proactively rather than waiting
  • Use junior residents as teaching opportunities: explain your reasoning, quiz them
  • Same EMR (Wellsky/ECS) as St. Catherine's — the systems will feel familiar
  • Recommended reading: Braddom chapters on spasticity, SCI, and TBI

📸 Attending Headshots

Highly recommended before you start: Read the Larkin WPB VA PGY4 Rotation Guide written by a PGY-4 who just completed this rotation — covers access setup, EMG workflow, Cadwell/Sierra tips, and more.

Overview

The WPB VA is primarily an Electrodiagnostics (EDx) rotation running Monday–Friday. Residents participate in EMG/NCS studies with VA attendings throughout the week. Optionally, residents can also work in the MSK clinic, which includes PRP, Botox, IAS injections, and consults — the only dedicated MSK clinic day is Thursday afternoon with Dr. Cuevas.

Start VA credentialing paperwork 6–8 weeks in advance — delays are common and you cannot start without clearance. Contact Dr. Garcia-Negron early to initiate the process.

📍 Logistics

  • Facility: Thomas H. Corey VA Medical Center (formerly the West Palm Beach VA Medical Center)
  • Address: 7305 North Military Trail, West Palm Beach, FL 33410-7417
  • Location: 3rd floor, Pain Management Suite, opposite the PM&R department.
  • Service: PM&R Consult Service + Outpatient Clinic + EDX
  • EMR: VistA / CPRS (VA-specific; plan for a learning curve)
  • Schedule: M–F; no overnight call (VA hours, ~8 AM–4:30 PM)
  • Residents: PGY-3 and PGY-4
  • Dress: Business professional / white coat / Scrubs

👥 Key Contacts

📋 Pre-Rotation Credentialing Steps

These steps must be completed before your rotation start date. Allow 6–8 weeks minimum.

  • Email Dr. Garcia-Negron (jorge.garcia-negron2@va.gov) to begin the credentialing process
  • Complete VA credentialing application
  • Complete required VA onboarding modules
  • Obtain VA PIV card (photo ID) — scheduled at VA HR
  • Get VA network/CPRS access set up by IT
  • Register for VA VPN if remote access needed

📅 Weekly Schedule

Day AM PM
Monday Dr. Fitzig – EMG Didactics (excused)
Tuesday Dr. Reddy – EMG TBD (previously Dr. Woo)
Wednesday Dr. Garcia Negron – EMG Dr. Cuevas – EMG
Thursday Dr. Reid-Artist – EMG Dr. Cuevas – MSK (Botox, PRP, IAS, consults)
Friday Dr. Garcia – EMG Dr. Reid-Artist – EMG

EDx runs every day Monday–Friday. Thursday afternoon with Dr. Cuevas is the only dedicated MSK clinic. Outside of that, MSK/PRP/Botox opportunities are optional and available when time permits.

📝 Daily Structure

  1. Open patient in CPRS → review EMG consult
  2. Set up Cadwell/Sierra for the study
  3. Perform EMG/NCS with attending
  4. Write and co-sign note in CPRS
  5. Thursday PM: MSK clinic with Dr. Cuevas (Botox, PRP, IAS, consults)
  6. Free time: explore MSK/PRP, interventional spine and pain, P&O, acupuncture, pelvic rehab

🎓 Didactics Attendance

Didactics attendance is required while on the VA rotation. You must join via video conference call on scheduled didactic days. Failure to attend and actively participate will count as a recorded absence.

✅ Rotation Expectations

  • Complete VA credentialing before start date (initiate 6–8 weeks early)
  • Learn CPRS/VistA EMR and EMG note workflow during first week
  • Participate in EMG/NCS studies daily with assigned attending
  • Complete and co-sign EDx notes in CPRS for every study
  • Attend Thursday PM MSK clinic with Dr. Cuevas
  • Attend didactics via video conference (Monday AM)
  • Track your daily schedule on a blank calendar — Dr. Reid-Artist will request this at some point during the rotation
  • Journal club (monthly): you are excused — just notify your attending in advance

📚 Learning Objectives

  • EMG/NCS technique and interpretation (primary focus)
  • CPRS/VistA documentation for EDx studies
  • Feltsenthal and Stevens criteria for nerve comparisons
  • Cadwell/Sierra machine operation
  • MSK procedures: PRP, Botox, IAS injections (Thursday PM)
  • Veteran-specific diagnoses (polytrauma, TBI, MSK injuries)

📄 VA EMG/NCS Note Templates (CPRS) — Copy-paste ready templates for all EDX studies at the VA. Includes UE/LE EMG tables, full procedure notes, component blocks, and signature template.

VA EDX / EMG-NCS Templates (CPRS)

📖 EDX Lunchtime Lecture Articles

These 22 articles are required for resident presentations during the EDX/MSK rotation. Confer with Dr. Reid-Artist to determine which articles you will be presenting.

  1. Identifying Lumbosacral Radiculopathies. An Optimal Electromyographic Screen. Am J Phys Med Rehabil 2000; 79:496-503

  2. Identification of Cervical Radiculopathies: Optimizing the Electromyography Screen. AM J Phys Med Rehabil 2001; 80:84-91

Overview

ISS (Integrative Spine & Sports) is your primary outpatient PM&R rotation. High volume of MSK, spine, and sports medicine patients across two clinic locations. This is where you build clinical efficiency, patient throughput, and procedure confidence.

Hours & Preparation

  • Weekdays generally start at 8–9 AM. Residents split Saturday half-day shifts; organize coverage with the seniors.
  • Bring: Laptop and reflex hammer. Dress: Scrubs.
  • On day one, obtain a thorough orientation from the office manager. Allow extra commute time and notify the office and co-residents if delayed.

📝 Clinic Workflow

  1. Review patient schedule the night before
  2. See patients independently (new and follow-up)
  3. Present to Dr. Diaz for review and sign-off
  4. Assist or perform procedures under supervision
  5. Write WRS notes immediately after each encounter when possible. If interrupted, record procedures, equipment, and medications used so documentation and coding can be completed accurately.

Room & Equipment Workflow

  • In WRS, blue patient names indicate arrival; confirm room assignment with the senior resident.
  • Established visits may include e-stim/heat, interval history, medication response and side effects, OMT, and requested procedures under attending guidance. Ask a senior to orient you to equipment.
  • For new patients, complete an H&P and develop a differential, workup, and treatment plan before presenting to Dr. Diaz.
  • After the visit, replace used sheets, place laundry appropriately, and remove/unplug cords that could create trip hazards.

Teaching & Student Rotators

  • Medical students take histories, document, and observe procedures; students must not perform needle sticks or independent procedures.
  • Residents must see their own patients and write their own notes. Each resident should write more notes daily than an individual student, excluding encounters where the resident supervises the student.
  • Seniors should arrange short teaching presentations 2–3 times weekly; the student onboarding template also asks each rotator to present a rehab/pain topic weekly.

  • Student arrival instructions: 8:15 AM, scrubs without a white coat, student ID, laptop, and charger. Park closer to the street to preserve convenient post-office parking.
  • Ask students to review neuromuscular/MSK examination, common peripheral nerve injuries, and multimodal pain treatment before arrival.

Documentation & Coding Clarification

Match diagnoses to documented services, including procedure medications. Incomplete notes or coding may jeopardize rotation completion. Confirm Medicare Part B modality billing requirements with Dr. Diaz and the billing team before submitting charges.

Patient facesheet: Each morning, scan facesheet → email to all three ISS office contacts above (same process as Larkin South inpatient)

Overview

The EDX rotation spans multiple sites (ISS, South Florida Spine & Wellness, and the WPB VA) and covers nerve conduction studies (NCS) and electromyography (EMG). One of the most technically demanding PM&R skills — start studying before the rotation begins.

📍 Sites

Site Address EMR
ISS — Fort Lauderdale 3308 NE 34th St, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33308 WRS
South Florida Spine & Wellness 3000 SW 148th Street, Suite 115, Miramar, FL 33027 — South Florida Spine and Sports; office: (954) 438-7000 N/A
West Palm Beach VA 7305 N Military Trail, West Palm Beach, FL 33410 CPRS/VistA

📅 Weekly EDX Schedule

Day Location Attending
Tuesday South Florida Spine & Wellness One resident at 8 AM with Dr. Fishman; the other at 9 AM with Dr. Romero. Switch assignments weekly.
Wednesday West Palm Beach VA VA Attendings (Garcia-Negron, Reid-Artist, etc.)
Thursday West Palm Beach VA VA Attendings
Friday ISS — Fort Lauderdale Dr. Diaz

👥 Key Contacts

Site Attending Contact
ISS Jose Diaz, DO drjosejuandiaz@gmail.com
South FL Spine Mark Fishman, MD TBD
South FL Spine Francisco Romero, MD TBD
VA Jorge E. Garcia-Negron, MD jorge.garcia-negron2@va.gov
VA Jacinth Reid-Artist, MD; Francisco J. Garcia, MD; Srinivas Reddy, MD; Ramon L. Cuevas-Trisan, MD; Jeremy Fitzig, DO TBD

📝 Site Workflow & Coverage

  • Duration: Average 3 months; may vary. Dress: Scrubs.
  • Coordinate a weekly schedule with your co-resident; alternate VA attendance on Wednesday/Thursday.
  • Dr. Fishman: Review charts before encounters and observe studies.
  • Dr. Romero: Observe ultrasound initially, with increasing responsibility toward scanning independently by the end of the rotation.
  • ISS: Check WRS weekly, usually Thursday, or contact ISS residents to confirm Friday EMGs. Both EMG residents must attend Friday when a study is scheduled. An ISS EMG takes priority even if scheduled on another weekday.
  • At ISS, perform the complete NCS/EMG study and review the results with Dr. Diaz; a senior ISS resident can assist when needed.
  • ISS coverage: EMG residents may be called to help cover ISS; coordinate with ISS residents.
  • VA coverage: Chiefs may assign coverage on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday when no ISS EMG is scheduled.
  • Additional reading: Liveson’s Peripheral Neurology: Case Studies, The McLean Course in Electrodiagnostic Medicine, and Easy EMG (Weiss, Silver, and Weiss).

🧠 Core EDX Skills to Master

Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)

  • Motor NCS: median, ulnar, peroneal, tibial
  • Sensory NCS: median, ulnar, radial, sural, superficial peroneal
  • F-waves and H-reflexes
  • Latency, amplitude, conduction velocity interpretation

Electromyography (EMG)

  • Insertional activity, spontaneous activity (fibs, PSW, CRD, fasciculations)
  • Motor unit action potential (MUAP) morphology
  • Recruitment patterns (early, reduced, discrete)
  • Key muscles for root/plexus/peripheral nerve localization

📚 Common Diagnoses

  • Carpal tunnel syndrome
  • Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow
  • Radiculopathies (cervical: C5–C8; lumbar: L4–S1)
  • Polyneuropathy (diabetic, length-dependent)
  • Plexopathies (brachial, lumbosacral)
  • ALS / motor neuron disease red flags

✅ Rotation Expectations

  • Perform NCS independently under supervision
  • Needle EMG under attending supervision
  • Write complete EDX reports
  • Log all studies in New Innovations
  • Pass EDX competency assessment before end of rotation

📚 Study Resources

  • Preston & Shapiro: Electromyography and Neuromuscular Disorders
  • AANEM primer on EDX medicine
  • Practice NCS calculation worksheets
  • Braddom Chapter on EDX

⚠️ Tips & Pitfalls

  • Start studying EDX before the rotation begins — steep learning curve
  • Skin temperature matters: cold limbs slow conduction — warm the patient first
  • Always correlate EDX findings with clinical exam and imaging
  • Learn normal values by heart (median motor DL, sural amplitude, etc.)
  • At the VA: EMG room has a max capacity limit — coordinate scheduling in advance
  • Each site has a different EMG machine — get oriented on day 1 at each site

Pediatric PM&R — Part I is a 1-month rotation at Nationwide Children's Hospital (NCH) in Columbus, Ohio. This is a fully immersive pediatric rehab experience covering CP, spina bifida, TBI, neuromuscular disease, and pediatric sports injuries. You will be away from home for this rotation.

🧠 Common Diagnoses

  • Cerebral palsy (spastic, dyskinetic, ataxic, mixed)

  • Duchenne and other muscular dystrophies
  • Pediatric TBI and ABI

Day-to-Day Experience

  • Split your time between inpatient and outpatient care. Attendings rotate among inpatient, outpatient, and consult services, providing opportunities to work with different faculty.
  • OSU PM&R residents also rotate here: a PGY-2 is assigned to inpatient and a PGY-3 is assigned to outpatient. Share the inpatient census with the OSU resident.
  • A prior resident reported an inpatient cap of 3 patients, allowing time to finish notes and follow-up before afternoon clinic. Confirm your assigned census with the attending.
  • Outpatient clinics have multiple attendings and patients shared with the OSU outpatient resident. Experiences include multidisciplinary myelodysplasia and CP clinics, concussion clinic, Botox procedures, and EMG when scheduled.
  • Some attendings offer informal lunchtime lectures and will let you know when they occur.

Inpatient Rehabilitation — H9B

From the main entrance, turn right and find the hallway with lockers. Badge through the door into the employee hallway, turn left, and continue to the third set of elevators—farther down the hall than you may expect, with three elevators in that area. Take the elevator to the 9th floor.

General / Concussion / Botox / NATBI — T1A

These clinics are in the first-floor PM&R clinic, across from urgent care.

  • General / concussion: See patients and write notes on a few patients each clinic under attending guidance.
  • NATBI (nonaccidental TBI): Often multidisciplinary with PM&R, psychology, and social work.
  • Botox: Opportunities to assist depend on the attending and how many days you work with them.

Myelo Clinic

Located at the far end of the hospital near the orange garage. Typically follow a patient through the multidisciplinary visits to understand each specialty’s care plan: PM&R, neurosurgery, GI, urology, PT/OT, social work, and others.

EMG — H10A

On the 10th floor, A side, one floor above inpatient rehab but on the opposite side. Through the double doors, look to the right for a workstation area with a door into the EMG room. Attend only when scheduled; there may be one or two patients before you move to another clinic.

CP & Seating Clinics — LOSC / Ortho Building

  • CP clinic: 5th floor; multidisciplinary with PM&R, orthopedics, neurosurgery, PT/OT, social work, and others.
  • Seating clinic: 2nd floor; with the attending, PT, and seating company.
  • Approximately a 7-minute walk from the main hospital. A parking garage is available if driving, or arrange a direct rideshare.
  • Enter on the north side of the LOSC building; there is no direct entrance from Livingston Avenue.

Hospital Maps

📚 Learning Objectives

  • Pediatric developmental milestones and assessment
  • GMFCS, MACS, CFCS classification systems
  • Spasticity management in children (weight-based dosing, site selection)
  • Orthotics and assistive technology for pediatric patients
  • Family-centered care principles
  • Epic EMR in a pediatric hospital setting
  • Become comfortable with pediatric rehabilitation treatments, including therapies, medications, and orthotics.
  • Use available time to read about patients’ conditions, observe their deficits, and understand differences between pediatric and elderly rehabilitation care.

  • PM&R Pocketpedia
  • Cuccurullo

⚠️ Tips & Pitfalls

  • Always communicate with parents/guardians — they are the primary historians
  • Botulinum toxin dosing in children is weight-based and differs significantly from adults
  • Pediatric patients vary widely — a 4-year-old and a 16-year-old require very different approaches
  • GMFCS levels guide prognosis and therapy goals — know all 5 levels
  • Contact Leah Settles early for NCH credentialing — out-of-state hospitals have longer processing times

Overview

The Dr. Hatgis elective is an interventional pain rotation at Interventional Spine Specialists of Florida (ISSF), with offices in Tamarac and Plantation, FL. It is one of the most procedure-dense electives available — highly recommended for residents interested in spine, pain medicine, or outpatient musculoskeletal practice.

📍 Logistics

  • Practice: Interventional Spine Specialists of Florida (ISSF)
  • Attending: Jesse Hatgis, DO
  • Tamarac Office: 7171 N. University Dr., Ste. 300, Tamarac, FL
  • Plantation Office: 499 NW 70th Ave., Ste. 200, Plantation, FL
  • Contact: 1 month prior via email (contact through clinic)
  • Schedule: M–F, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM; procedures on Friday AM

📅 Weekly Schedule

Day Activity
Monday Clinic with Dr. Hatgis
Tuesday Work with PAs
Wednesday Work with PAs
Thursday Clinic with Dr. Hatgis
Friday Clinic with Dr. Hatgis + Procedures (AM)

📝 Clinic Workflow

  1. Arrive on time for clinic and outpatient surgery days; read beforehand and stay engaged with visits and procedures.
  2. The MA gathers a brief history. Review that information, confirm it with the patient, and perform a short, focused physical examination.
  3. Discuss the likely plan with the patient, then present to the PA or Dr. Hatgis. Return together to communicate the final plan.
  4. Keep encounters focused and efficient. Learn the low-back-pain treatment algorithms used by the PAs.
  5. Observe procedures initially. As anatomy and spine knowledge improve, Dr. Hatgis may allow assistance with procedures such as medial branch blocks and epidural injections.
  6. Maintain your procedure log.

🩺 Procedures

  • Medial branch blocks (MBBs)
  • Epidural injections — transforaminal, interlaminar, caudal
  • Facet joint injections
  • Spinal cord stimulator (SCS) implants
  • PRP injections
  • Discograms
  • Endoscopic rhizotomy
  • MILD procedure
  • Peripheral nerve stimulation

The new surgery center is awaiting certification by an accrediting body. Lauderdale Lakes Surgical Center is no longer accepting residents or fellows to observe or participate in procedures.

📚 Recommended Reading

  • Review all epidural approaches: transforaminal, interlaminar, caudal

Residents must be formally dismissed by the attending physician before leaving their assigned duties for the day. Walking out without proper dismissal is not permitted.

Larkin South / Waterford (PGY-2)

  • Sunday: new admissions only

📣 Communication Expectations

policies.title: Grievances & Due Process
policies.html:
Grievances & Due Process

Purpose: To provide residents with reasonable written institutional policies and procedures for Grievance and Due Process.

This disciplinary process does not create a contractual obligation to use progressive discipline in every case. The sponsoring institution has the right to discipline any inappropriate conduct without progressing through all levels.

👥 Key Definitions

Term Definition
DIO Designated Institutional Official — physician with oversight, administration, and accountability for residency programs
ADME Administrative Director of Medical Education — manages administrative functions of the GME Division
GMEC Graduate Medical Education Committee — comprises the DIO, Program Directors, Peer-Selected Resident Representatives, Faculty Representatives, and administration
Disciplinary Committee Standing committee of the GMEC that reviews extensions of Concern Status, Probation, and Termination
Program Director Physician responsible for managing the residency program

📋 Progressive Discipline Ladder

1️⃣ Coaching

  • Non-threatening conversation between resident and supervising attending
  • Intent: improve performance or professional conduct
  • Not appealable

2️⃣ Oral Counseling

  • First level of formal disciplinary notice by supervising attending
  • Discussion held with resident; documents the problem and suggests corrective action
  • Constitutes a formal warning
  • Not appealable (may be discussed via Informal Dispute process)

3️⃣ Written Reprimand

  • Issued by Supervising Physician or Program Director; must be in writing
  • Must include: resident name, persons present, reason for reprimand, incident description, dates, prior discipline, signature lines (resident, attending, PD, DIO copy)
  • Resident signing acknowledges receipt only, not agreement
  • Not appealable (may be discussed via Informal Dispute process)

4️⃣ Concern Status

  • Formal discipline less serious than Probation
  • Imposed by Program Director for up to 6 months
  • PD must notify Department Chair and DIO; Disciplinary Committee notified in writing
  • Extensions or escalation to Probation requires Disciplinary Committee approval
  • PD evaluates resident monthly during Concern Status

Types of Concern Status:

Type Description
Clinical Concern Unsatisfactory performance on clinical portions of the program
Academic Concern Unsatisfactory performance on knowledge-based portions
Professional Concern Behaviors calling into question clinical, personal, or moral attributes related to fitness to practice

5️⃣ Probation

  • Period of critical examination to determine if resident may continue in the program
  • May be preceded by Concern Status, or imposed directly for serious circumstances
  • Imposed for up to 3 months by the Disciplinary Committee; extensions require Committee approval
  • PD evaluates resident monthly during Probation

6️⃣ Termination for Cause

  • The Disciplinary Committee may decide termination
  • PD writes recommendation to Disciplinary Committee → Committee adopts/disapproves/modifies → DIO has final authority
  • This is the only level that is appealable

🏋️ Academic Discipline

Unsatisfactory academic performance is defined as:

  • Failed rotation
  • In-service exam scores below program requirements (below 40th percentile on annual in-service exam)
  • Marginal or unsatisfactory faculty evaluations in: clinical diagnosis/judgment, medical knowledge, technical abilities, patient management, communication skills, professionalism, attendance, or motivation

Academic Probation: Residents with unsatisfactory academic performance undergo a probationary period with:

  1. Written notice of performance deficiencies
  2. Opportunity to remedy deficiencies (remediation plan)
  3. Specified probationary period

Possible outcomes after academic probation:

  • Removal from probation (return to good standing)
  • Continued probation with new/remaining deficiencies
  • Non-promotion to next training level
  • Contract non-renewal
  • Dismissal

📎 Disciplinary Forms

  • Concern Status Form
  • Written Reprimand Form

🛡️ Prohibition Against Retaliation

The sponsoring institution is committed to preventing any retaliation against persons who raise legitimate questions regarding their employment in good faith. Supervisors are expected to take time to answer questions and work toward resolution of workplace concerns.

📚 Reference

See the Larkin GME Resident Handbook for the full grievance policy, appeals process, and complete Disciplinary Committee procedures.

St. Anthony’s Addendum: A day in the life of a PGY3/4 resident at SA

Attending: Dr. Queiroz “Dr. Q” (Phone Number: 205-835-4655)

Census: 22 rooms total. 201-222. Some rooms have multiple beds.

Hours: 8AM to 12PM, Q would like for us to be present in the hospital until noon every day. He does not require both residents to be there, however. Be responsible and you can work out a good schedule amongst you and your coresident (i.e. 8-10 shift and 10-12 shift).

Rounding: Q shows up at random times in the day. Sometimes he will show up and round at 6 am by himself, does not expect you to be there at that time. Usually if there is a new patient, he will be there to see the patient during 8-12 and will ask the resident to present. You don’t have to see the patient with him or round completely with him, but did occasionally round on the new ones with him.

Team at 10 am on Monday and Friday and if necessary on Thursday for Monday night/Tuesday night admits. This is a new thing that just started this week so check w/ Dr. Q or Kristina (PPS coordinator) on final team days. She should be texting you both. Usually in the big conference room but sometimes in the small room. Just check w/ the nurses.

Obviously if you are splitting your shifts and you’re doing 10-12, you will need to come earlier on team days and be prepared for it. Again, use common sense and be responsible.

Same deal as SCW, same ECS and WellSky. You can check WellSky night before to see if any new patients have been admitted so you have an idea and split the admissions if need be. You can also call the facility at night and ask the night nurses if there have been any admissions as other residents have done in the past.

Sidenote: WellSky does not work well on iPhone Safari or Chrome, it’s pretty much not navigable.

Weekends are same as SCW. Alternating weekends. Usually covered with Dr. Q. Sometimes his NP does come on weekends but rarely. Her name is Mariela Rios 786-319-6537.

Q expects you to see all the patients and new admissions regardless and write notes on all of them on Saturdays, regardless of cap. Sunday coverage only if new patient then you are responsible to write H/P just on that patient.

What’s the difference between SCW and SA?

Patient population is English speaking primarily and smaller overall patient load. Will have Creole speaking patients here and there. A lot of the nurses are Creole speaking so just ask for help if you need translation.

Q gives you way more independence to order whatever (within reason and available at SA) you think is best for your patient for management/treatment/consultants.

You do not need to run everything by him as long as you keep him informed.

No one is checking your orders like Feliz and Neubert were, so be diligent and don’t make mistakes. The nurses are good and they will catch things for you if things are ordered in the wrong chart or duplicate orders, but still.

If you place an order for a controlled substance:

You will need to place the order in ECS and you will need to write a rx using the prescription pad (located in bin behind nursing station), usually put the quantity as 30 tabs and let the nurses know. If you forget to do it, the nursing also will write these scripts out and leave them for Q, but it’s a good habit to just do them yourself.

You will need to do discharge med recs for upcoming discharges:

Go to “view/edit current orders”, select every med that you want to discharge patient on (the text goes red, you don’t need to shift click or control click). Once they are all selected (double check because its really easy to accidentally unclick on something or mis-select) right click and select “append all”  it will go to the order screen, click on "Print Rx providers only” blue box 

all you have to do is wait, it will say prescription printed or something and then the screen will close on its own to the main ECS screen  on the main ECS screen on the bottom right there is a blue box “Print Rx”, select it, choose patient, choose today, and you’ll see the prescriptions  hit print (always print to SJW printer)  once printed, on the top of the first page of the scripts write down your NPI number  go through each script and place the correct quantity with units and sign the script. Refills are 0. Usually give patients 30 day supply unless its controlled. (make sure you’re doing the math correctly because the patients outside pharmacy will call you and clarify if it doesn't make sense)

If patients are on controlled substances and being discharged on them

You cannot discharge it as a normal prescription on ECS. It needs to be written on a prescription pad. All controlled substances will only be given for 3 days quantity, again do the math. Don’t sign the script, leave it for Dr Q to sign.

***IF you have your own DEA number, you can sign the script with your own DEA number obviously

If patient is being discharged over the weekend, have the controlled substance script written by Friday so Q can have it signed.

IMPORTANT: If patient is leaving tomorrow and patient is on controlled substances that will require Dr Q’s signature do the written script at the minimum the day prior so that he will sign in the morning if he comes early. If you do it the day of discharge and the patient needs a controlled substance rx and Q already came for the day, they are SOL.

You will lead team conference, Q will show you the ropes the first couple of times. But basically, you are to report any medical barriers to discharge for the patient. I usually just give any pertinent details for IV abx timings or status changes; important labs and what's being done for them. If it's the first conference for this patient, I usually will just give a quick one liner or state the Dx so everyone's on the same page. Listen and be interactive. The therapists or Q may ask you questions about the patient occasionally so be mentally present.

Nurses are great; they know about the flow and what you can and cannot order. Josee is the nursing supervisor, she is super helpful and can find you answers to everything basically.

There is no IRL lab login available; Just check labs on ECS. No MDops login either; consultant notes are printed and placed in the chart, but I usually just check orders on ECS and figure it out.

Most common consultants:

Neuro: Wilson. Cardio: Urbandt. Contact Stephanie (NP) for anything Cards related your needed. Nephro: Rosario. Contact Anna (NP) for anything Nephro related you needed. NP: Rose. Pulm: Liebermann/Chaudhry. Psych: Carlos (Balanced Wellbeing). Palliative: Bloom Palliative (let CM know). ID: Chaudhari (Contact NP Shobha/Faisal for ID related stuff. The NPs alternate weeks)

Check w/ Q which IM doc he wants (been drama in the past). Usually if they are coming from Westside, its Sardinas (Greg NP comes) but just check with Q. Rock (NP) works w/ Dr. Golalwala and Dr. Mendez

Radiology site available: pmdxu.com \\ User: SAhospital | Password: Pass1!

Nurses will also print out radiology reports; you need to sign to acknowledge that you read it.

Overall chill rotation, a good place to gain independence and confidence. Q is a good attending, and he is smart and actually helpful (most of the time).

SEPT 2026

Part 1: Getting Access Set Up

1. PIV Card and Windows Access

Use your PIV card and PIN to log into VA computers.

If Windows says your account is disabled, call IT. They may ask someone with an active VA email — such as another resident — to verify your identity using a code.

2. Microsoft Office 365 and CPRS

Open YourIT and request Microsoft Office 365 for Outlook and Teams. Access is usually available by your next login.

For CPRS, open VA Shortcuts and select CPRSChart WPB. Create a desktop shortcut if helpful.

3. Patient Check-In and Clinic Lists

In Edge, open:

VA Bookmarks → VHA → Patient Check In, Clinical Staff View

Favorite the page and create a desktop shortcut.

Create these lists:

  • EMG: Add all EMG attendings using the CPRS clinic designations to view appointments and check-in status.
  • Pain/MSK/PRP: Track these clinics without searching each one in CPRS.

Keep the EMG list open on the second monitor. If a patient appears to be a no-show, call for them before assuming they are absent. If you cannot access the application or receive an error code, submit an IT ticket.

Update as of 09/29/26: They changed the security protocol and we don't have access anymore. Ask Kendra or Dr. Garcia Negron for help. IT response: "PCI-CSV has started enforcing the security key requirement for access. You don't have the necessary keys needed to access PCI-CSV. Please see your Supervisor or ADPAC to gain access via EPAS."

4. Creating Your CPRS Electronic Signature Code

Your CPRS electronic signature code is separate from your PIV PIN and must be created through VistA. Recommend making your signature code the same as your CPRS login for simplicity.

  1. Open VistA through Gold Star or VA Shortcuts and select the appropriate VistA option.
  2. At the Main Menu, enter TB or Toolbox.
  3. At Select User's Toolbox, enter ELE.
  4. Verify or update:
    • Initials: Legal initials, ALL CAPS.
    • Signature Block Printed Name: Full legal name, ALL CAPS.
    • Signature Block Title: Title, ALL CAPS.
    • Office Phone: VA office or facility number, not your personal cell.
    • Voice Pager/Digital Pager: Review as applicable.
  5. If REPLACE appears when editing your title, enter ..., press Enter, then re-enter the title in ALL CAPS when prompted with WITH.
  6. Create a code when prompted:
    • 6–20 characters or numbers
    • ALL UPPERCASE
    • No characters requiring the Ctrl key
    • Your typing will not appear on screen
  7. Re-enter the code to verify it.
  8. Press Enter repeatedly to exit the Toolbox.

If you bypass the signature prompt or enter the confirmation incorrectly, return to the Main Menu and repeat the process.

Set this up early. Keep the code private and out of your note templates.

Part 2: Schedule and Responsibilities

5. Weekly Schedule

Monday–Friday; no weekends. Lunch is 12–1 PM, and afternoon clinics begin at 1 PM.

Day AM PM
Monday Dr. Fitzig – EMG Didactics (excused)
Tuesday Dr. Reddy – EMG TBD; previously Dr. Woo
Wednesday Dr. Garcia Negron – EMG Dr. Cuevas – EMG
Thursday Dr. Reid-Artist – EMG Dr. Cuevas – MSK
Friday Dr. Garcia – EMG Dr. Reid-Artist – EMG

Thursday afternoons with Dr. Cuevas may include MSK, Botox, EMG-guided Botox, and migraine management. Confirm the Tuesday afternoon schedule after you start.

6. CPRS Clinic Assignments

Search WPB Rehab EMG in CPRS.

Clinic Attending
I Dr. Fitzig
II Dr. Reddy
III Dr. Reid-Artist
IV Dr. Garcia Negron
V Dr. Cuevas
VI Dr. Garcia
X Dr. Woo (former)

7. General Expectations

All scheduled EMG clinics are mandatory. Participate in the studies and complete the associated documentation.

During free time, explore MSK/PRP, interventional spine and pain, Dr. Garcia's pain suite, P&O, rehabilitation, acupuncture, and pelvic rehab.

8. Resident Presentations

The two PGY-4s and Broward EMG resident alternate presentations on Tuesdays and Fridays, approximately 12:15–12:50 PM.

Coordinate the schedule and keep Dr. Reid-Artist informed.

To schedule a presentation:

  1. Open Outlook → Calendar on the VA desktop.
  2. Create the meeting.
  3. Add a Teams link.
  4. Invite all attendings.

Email the PowerPoint to your VA email beforehand; Google Drive/Slides may be unreliable on VA computers.

Part 3: The EMG Workflow

9. Starting the EMG Machine

  1. Turn on the monitor.
  2. Turn on the Cadwell machine using the switch on the back left.
  3. Open Sierra and log in with username admin and password admin.
  4. Press Enter if another prompt appears.
  5. For a new patient, enter the first name, last name, and last four SSN digits as the patient ID. Attending and technician fields are optional.
  6. Click Start and select the appropriate template. Common templates: Bruno Upper Extremity, Bruno Lower Extremity, and Cuevas.

10. Opening the Patient in CPRS

  1. Select Clinic.
  2. Search WPB Rehab EMG.
  3. Select the appropriate numbered clinic.
  4. Choose the patient from the schedule.

Select Save Clinic for Current Day to avoid repeating the search.

Useful CPRS tabs:

  • Cover Sheet: PMH, medications, BMI.
  • Reports → Local Imaging: MRI and other imaging.
  • Labs: A1c and other relevant results.
  • Consults: EMG referral and related documentation.

11. Reviewing the EMG Consult

In Consults, open the most recent EMG referral. Review the referring provider, consultation reason, history, and any attending recommendations.

Before starting, determine which nerves to test based on the presentation. Attendings may have different preferences.

12. Setting Up CPRS Note Templates

Upper- and lower-extremity EMG templates and additional examination components are available.

To save a template:

  1. Open a patient chart and create a temporary note under Notes.
  2. Select Templates in the lower-left corner.
  3. Right-click → Create/Edit Template.
  4. Name the template and paste the text.
  5. Click Apply.
  6. Repeat as needed, then discard the temporary note.

Shared templates: Shared Template → Physical Medicine → PM&R Physicians → EDx. Consult note templates are also there.

Update resident names in the signature section and remove irrelevant attending names. To insert a component, place the cursor where you want it and double-click the template.

13. Starting an EMG Note and Answering the Consult

With the consult selected, go to:

Action → Consult Results → Complete/Update Results

Start the note through this pathway so it remains linked to the consult. Select the EMG note and assign the appropriate attending as co-signer.

If Consult Results is grayed out, request IT access for:

  • PAIN PROCEDURE OUTPATIENT
  • PHYSICAL MED & REHAB (EMG/NCS) OUTPATIENT
  • REHAB MD OUTPATIENT

Request the same permissions as your co-resident. Dr. Garcia-Negron may also help.

14. Writing the Note

Referring provider and consult reason: In Orders, open the EMG order and copy the referring provider and exact consultation reason. Use Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V; right-click copying may not work.

HPI: Update age, sex, handedness, and focused history. Ask about symptom onset/progression, diabetes, thyroid disease, alcohol use, prior treatments, and previous EMG/NCS studies.

If a prior VA study exists, locate its numerical results for comparison. Use the Snipping Tool only within approved VA systems.

Use Save Without Signature to preserve an unfinished note.

15. Recording and Interpreting Results

Align numerical values carefully, especially decimal points under the correct L/R designations.

Finding Wording
Latency Prolonged
Amplitude Low
Conduction velocity Slow/Slowed

Match singular/plural wording to the number of nerves or muscles tested.

Interpret each nerve as you complete it and mark completed interpretations with an asterisk. Review the Feltsenthal and Stevens criteria, especially median–ulnar and median–radial comparisons.

16. Signing Your Note

Select the correct attending as co-signer.

Do not designate yourself as the primary provider. When prompted, select No or change the primary provider to the attending. This keeps the note associated with the attending for future retrieval.

Sign using your CPRS electronic signature code.

Part 4: Cadwell/Sierra Tips

17. Probe Controls

Wipe gel from the probe ends between patients. Alcohol swabs work well.

Control Function
Scroll wheel Adjusts stimulus intensity
1 Distance entry
2 Advances to the next nerve
3 Turns averaging on/off
+/− Changes polarity
Store Saves the selected waveform
- Distance (1): Press 1, scroll to enter the distance in centimeters, then press Store or 1 to advance.
- Next nerve (2): Advances through the study list. Arrange nerves in performance order to use this efficiently.
- Averaging (3): Toggles averaging. The Average indicator highlights when active. The Cadwell machine also has an averaging button marked by an X with a bar over it.
- Polarity (+/−): Changes stimulus polarity. The green probe light indicates current direction. For routine NCS, direct current toward the recording electrodes; F-waves and H-reflexes are exceptions.

Important: Switching nerves resets stimulus intensity and polarity.

18. Organizing the Nerve List

Drag nerves to arrange the study order. You can move completed nerves to the top to distinguish them from pending studies.

19. Saving, Deleting, and Sorting Waveforms

Press Store to save a waveform; it changes from white to purple.

To delete multiple saved waveforms:

  1. Hold Ctrl and select the purple waveforms.
  2. Press Delete and confirm.
  3. Press F5 or select Sort Traces/Sort Waves to reorder by latency.

F5 works from the Cadwell machine or keyboard. Unstored white waveforms can be deleted directly.

20. Selecting a Previous Trace

Use the multiple-waveform icon next to the star in the upper-right corner to retrieve a prior trace.

  1. Click the icon.
  2. Select the desired trace; it turns yellow.
  3. Choose the option to replace the current trace.

Select only one trace. Selecting two causes Sierra to average them into a blue trace.

21. Adding Nerves or Additional Studies

To add a nerve, right-click the nerve list and select Insert, or use the star icon.

To add a study, select the star icon → Studies, then choose the template.

Confirm the correct laterality. If a study is labeled incorrectly, right-click the nerve and select the option to swap sides; repeating the study is unnecessary if the testing was performed correctly.

22. End-of-Day Shutdown

Turn off the Cadwell machine using the switch on the back left and turn off the monitor. Do not shut down the computer.
